title: Load three pans into an oven with the liquid pan on the lowest runners
instruction: Load the three pans from the counter into the oven, one pan on each runner level. The brown pan is stock, a liquid: it goes on the lowest runners, so it cannot spill or boil over into food below, and it must be kept level all the way. The roast and the vegetables go on the two levels above it. Slide each pan in from the front, resting on its two runners.
context: Commercial kitchen practice for multi-level ovens and racks puts liquids, sauces and stocks on the lowest runners: a spill or boil-over then cannot drip into food below, and hot liquid is never pulled out at face height, a common scald hazard; ovens are loaded from the bottom up. Cooks load gastronorm pans on side runners by sliding them in from the front. The skill is choosing the level by the rule and keeping the liquid level throughout, checked every step. Unlike RoboCasa ToastOnCorrectRack (the rack is named in the instruction) and TK-D9SEQ6 (raw meat on the bottom fridge shelf, placed from above), the level here follows from what the pan holds and each pan has to be slid onto its runners at its own height. Done by: cooks, restaurant and institution; food preparation workers (O*NET 35-2014.00, 35-2012.00, 35-2021.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), everything square to the table. Oven: an open-top, open-front cavity running from x 30 to 44, centred at y 26.5: fixed steel side walls (0.6 cm thick, 17 cm tall) with inner faces 5.9 cm either side of the centreline, a back wall at x 44 and a dark floor plate. On each side wall, fixed runners 1.2 cm wide and 0.4 cm thick along the full depth, at three levels (runner tops 2.5, 9 and 14 cm above the table); the runners' inner edges are 4.7 cm from the centreline, so a pan rests 8 mm on each. Counter: a fixed steel plate 11 x 40 cm, 0.4 cm thick, centred at x 17, y 26.5. Pans: boxes 7 cm deep (x) by 11 cm wide, standing on the counter at x 17: the stock pan (brown, 4 cm tall, 250 g) at y 26.5, the roast pan (dark red, 2 cm tall, 150 g) at y 39, the vegetable pan (green, 2 cm tall, 150 g) at y 14.
scoring: From the episode's recorded poses, with the grippers open at the end. A pan is on a level when it is still, level within 3 degrees, square within 5 degrees, its centre within 1.5 cm of x 36 and 5 mm of the oven's centreline, and its bottom within 3 mm of that level's runner tops. 0.5 for the stock pan on the lowest level; 0.25 for each of the roast and vegetable pans on level 2 or 3. If the stock pan ends on level 2 or 3, or ever tips more than 10 degrees during the trial, the score is capped at 0.25. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Success: score 1, held 1 s.
reset_notes: Stand the three pans back on the counter at their marks (roast left, stock in the middle, vegetables right); the oven, runners and counter are fixed. On a real rig, use a pan with water for the stock and judge tipping from the trial video.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). A pan (real 1/3 gastronorm, 325 x 176 mm) is a closed box at about one third scale; the stock is a 250 g solid, so a spill is judged from the pan's tilt. The oven has no top, door or heat, and its runners are plain ledges. Pans are gripped on their front and back faces instead of by their rims.
